Read POD5 metadata and signals (optionally)

Source: R/read_pod5.R
read_pod5.Rd

Captures read metadata with raw or calibrated signal (if requested), using native indexed selection for given read ids (UUIDs).

Usage

read_pod5(
  file,
  read_ids = NULL,
  signal = FALSE,
  calibrated = FALSE,
  start_sample = 1,
  end_sample = Inf,
  first_read = 1,
  num_reads = Inf
)

Arguments

file

character or external pointer: POD5 path or open native reader

read_ids

character (default: NULL). Unique read UUIDs. NULL selects by row range.

signal

logical (default: FALSE). Include signal vectors in the returned list.

calibrated

logical (default: FALSE). Return signal in picoampers instead of ADC counts.

start_sample

numeric (default: 1). First signal sample, one-based and inclusive.

end_sample

numeric (default: Inf). Last signal sample, one-based and inclusive.

first_read

numeric (default: 1). First read in file order, one-based.

num_reads

numeric (default: Inf). Maximum number of reads. Cannot be combined with read_ids unless first_read and num_reads retain their defaults.

Value

If signal is FALSE, a plain metadata data frame. Otherwise, a named list with reads (metadata) and signal (vectors named by UUID). Raw signals are integer vectors. Calibrated signals are numeric vectors.

Details

Read identifiers are returned in requested order. Missing identifiers and duplicate selections throw errors. Without identifiers, reads follow file order. Metadata access alone never decompresses signal data. Sample intervals use R coordinates: one-based and inclusive. Bounds beyond a read are clipped; a start beyond the read yields an empty vector. Only overlapping compressed chunks are decoded. Universal interval applies to all selected reads. When a file contains repeated UUIDs, indexed selection returns one occurrence chosen by the native library. Use row ranges or process_pod5() to get every occurrence.

Read start_sample retains its original zero-based acquisition coordinate. Signal orientation remains acquisition order. Calibration is (raw_signal + calibration_offset) * calibration_scale in picoamperes.

Output memory grows with selected reads and samples. Use process_pod5() for bounded read groups. Native file mapping and the POD5 chunk cache also consume memory. Opening a reader caches batch boundaries, not signal vectors.

Dorado split children have new UUIDs that are not stored in original POD5 file. Use extract_pod5_signal_dorado() with parent and sample tags from Dorado SAM/BAM to extract their signal intervals.

See also

extract_pod5_signal

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
reads <- pod5R::read_pod5("reads.pod5")
out <- pod5R::read_pod5("reads.pod5", read_ids = reads$read_id[1:5],
signal = TRUE, calibrated = TRUE)
} # }
